Patterns

Whole screens rather than parts. Nothing here is a new component — each one is an arrangement of things from the other pages, written down because the arrangement is the decision, and because these are the screens every application needs and nobody enjoys designing twice.

Dashboards

A twelve-column grid of widgets. The discipline is in the hierarchy: the figures somebody checks every morning go across the top at a size that can be read from a standing position, and everything that needs interpretation goes below them.

Filters and results

A panel of facets beside a list. Two rules carry it: the result count updates as the filters change, and everything currently applied is repeated as removable chips above the results — because a filter somebody forgot they set is indistinguishable from a bug.

Chat

A scrolling log with a composer pinned beneath it. The log scrolls, not the page, so the composer never leaves. Consecutive messages from one person group into a run: one avatar, one name, one tail — repeating all three for every line is what makes a transcript unreadable.

Comment threads

Replies indent exactly once. Past one level the indentation eats the measure, so deeper replies render flat and lean on a mention to say what they are answering — which is also how they read on a phone, where there was never room to indent at all.

Boards

Columns of cards, where moving a card between columns is the edit. The board scrolls sideways and each column scrolls on its own — the only arrangement that survives both six columns and forty cards.

Backlog
  • Audit the color tokens against WCAG AA Design RK
  • Replace the bespoke date parser Tech debt JP
  • Write the migration note for v3 Docs MO
In progress
  • Focus trapping for the side sheet Blocked RK
  • Toolbar overflow on narrow screens Component AL
  • Right-to-left pass over the whole kit i18n SD
In review
  • Command palette keyboard contract Component JP
Done
  • Print stylesheet for the data table Shipped MO
  • Forced-colors audit Shipped SD

Drag a card with the pointer, or focus one and press Space: the arrow keys then move it up and down within a column and left and right between columns, Enter drops it and Esc puts it back where it started.

The card you grab comes with you — out of its column, under the pointer, with a dashed gap left in the place it would go back to. Hold it near the bottom of a column and that column scrolls; hold it near the left or right edge and the board scrolls sideways, and in a corner it does both at once, because the two directions are decided separately. A column that has run out hands the scrolling outward to the board rather than swallowing it. This is the same mechanism as the reorderable list — UI.lift(), one implementation — with the board adding only what is genuinely its own: the column a card is headed for, and a second axis to scroll. data-drag-proxy="off" on the board turns the carry off and leaves the drop lines.

Both routes exist because dragging is the obvious gesture and the one nobody can rely on. It wants a pointer, a steady hand, and a screen tall enough to show the source and the target at once — on a phone, with a tremor, or with a keyboard, it is simply unavailable. A board whose only affordance is drag-and-drop is a board some people cannot use at all.

Every move is announced through a live region, because a card quietly changing column is a change nobody listening to the page would otherwise know about. The "In progress" column carries data-limit="3", so its count turns amber when the work-in-progress limit is reached — the one number on a board that is worth drawing attention to.

Schedules

On a phone the month grid cannot show titles at any readable size, so each event becomes a dot and the detail moves to a day view underneath. A truncated title nobody can read is not a compromise, it is noise.

Authentication

Narrow, centerd and short. Every field here is one somebody has to get past before the product does anything for them, so the only things on the screen are the fields, the way out of a mistake, and the way to the other flow.

Error states

A region that failed inside an otherwise working page is not one of these. That is an alert in place, or an empty state with a retry — taking the whole screen away over one failed panel loses everything else that still worked.

Consent

Accept and reject carry equal weight. A reject hidden behind a settings link, or styled as a text link beside a filled accept, is a dark pattern — and in several jurisdictions, not valid consent.
